scope_note: Append-only S44 supplement. It does not edit curriculum source. Stable legacy id `multimodal` is preserved; defects arise where shared learner-facing surfaces incorrectly use that id as current semantic content.

components.current_content: The shared Theory playground indexes `demos[sectionId]`. For stable section id `multimodal`, the mapped learner-facing title is `Practica CLIP y Whisper (simulado)` and the code simulates multimodal concepts.
components.attack: Open S44 Theory using section id `multimodal`; the shared component resolves the obsolete pre-V3 demo even though S44 now teaches CI/CD and supply-chain security.
components.defense: The legacy id itself is a stable URL/progress key and should not be renamed casually.
components.verdict: The id is valid; using it as a semantic selector without a V3 override is not. Obsolete multimodal material leaks into the CI/CD lesson.
components.pedagogical_impact: The learner receives a topic switch inside Theory, breaks the mental model of the section, and may infer that CLIP/Whisper is part of the CI/CD objective.
components.improved_version: Keep `id: multimodal` for compatibility, but map the S44 Theory playground by a current semantic demo key or `section.index`. The S44 demo should inspect a small CI workflow/supply-chain manifest and derive pass/block from evidence.
components.justification: Separating stable identity from display semantics preserves progress while eliminating pre-V3 content leakage.

components.current_content: S44-T1-A references figure id `S44-permission-scope`. `FigureFrame` resolves only `FIGURES[figure.id]` or `FIGURE_DATA[figure.id]` and returns null when neither exists. `FIGURES` has no S44 permission figure; FIGURE_DATA is the union of flow/graph/misc data and none contains `S44-permission-scope`. The figure's caption is about tag-vs-SHA pinning and permissions although it is attached to T1-A matrices.
components.attack: Resolve `S44-permission-scope` through both registries. It is absent, so the intended learner visual never renders.
components.defense: S44-T1-A prose remains readable without the figure, and another S44 figure (`S44-supply-chain`) does exist.
components.verdict: The missing figure is a real render-path defect, not merely a caption preference. Its placement is also conceptually closer to T2-A than T1-A.
components.pedagogical_impact: A visual meant to clarify permission scope/pinning disappears entirely, removing a planned dual-coded explanation and leaving a silent gap in the rendered lesson.
components.improved_version: Either register a real `S44-permission-scope` figure and place it with T2-A, or remove the dead reference and use the existing supply-chain figure where it actually supports T1. Keep alt/caption aligned to the rendered visual.
components.justification: A referenced instructional figure must exist in the render registry; otherwise caption/alt never reaches the learner.

components.current_content: The canonical brief correctly says Gate S47, but its prerequisite line still names `S44 (multimodal), S45 (IaC), S46 (GPU computing), S47 (opensource)` while the V3 roadmap/current site titles are S44 CI/CD supply chain, S45 Cloud y colas, S46 Data eng producción, S47 MLOps serving.
components.attack: Compare the brief's human-readable prerequisite labels to learning_roadmap_52_V3.md and the current public section cards.
components.defense: The stable section identities can remain legacy internally, and the brief's gate number S47 is correct.
components.verdict: Learner-facing prerequisite names are stale and contradict the course they are taking. S44 self-check wording that calls an S44 check `el gate CP-N4-B` compounds the mismatch because the actual gate is S47.
components.pedagogical_impact: The learner cannot reliably understand what S44 contributes versus what is evaluated at S47, and may believe the current curriculum has missing/renamed sections.
components.improved_version: Update human-readable prerequisite labels to current V3 titles and say explicitly: `S44 inicia CP-N4-B; S47 ejecuta el gate canónico`.
components.justification: Stable identifiers and current labels are different concerns; learner-facing contracts must use current labels while preserving internal IDs separately.

components.current_content: Canonical CP-N4-B rubric uses 0-3 and weights correctness .35, robustness .20, maintainability .25, responsible_use .20 with weighted >=2.4, no critical criterion <2 and zero P0. S44 shows a different 25/20/15/15/15/10 percentage rubric without labeling it as an incremental S44 checkpoint.
components.attack: Score the same artifact under both schemes; pass/fail can differ.
components.defense: S44 is the start, not the closure, of CP-N4-B, so an interim rubric may legitimately differ.
components.verdict: The interim rubric is defensible only if explicitly labeled and mapped to the canonical S47 rubric. That bridge is absent.
components.pedagogical_impact: Learners cannot tell whether the visible score is formative S44 evidence or the actual capstone gate.
components.improved_version: Label the S44 rubric `checkpoint formativo S44` and map each criterion to the canonical CP-N4-B dimensions; link/quote the S47 gate rule separately.
components.justification: Formative and summative scoring can differ, but the relationship must be explicit to avoid contradictory assessment signals.

components.current_content: Authenticated exams sample one stored variant per concept. The S44 bank is updated to current CI/CD concepts, but examples such as `Una matrix de CI con Python 3.11 y 3.12 valida:` and `Fallar el pipeline si mypy/ruff fallan implementa:` are short recognition questions. The V3 roadmap separately requires four authentic topic assessments (two tasks per topic), which are not represented by the self-check or section MC exam.
components.attack: Compare assessment surfaces with the roadmap's required authentic per-topic tasks and Level-4 artifact-inspection demand.
components.defense: The section exam is allowed to use MC items, and the server correctly varies concepts/variants over attempts.
components.verdict: The bank is topically current but under-samples authentic artifact reasoning; more importantly, the four mandated topic assessments are absent.
components.pedagogical_impact: Recall can pass without demonstrating workflow inspection, artifact verification, environment protection or rollback evidence.
components.improved_version: Keep the section exam for retrieval practice, but add four roadmap-compliant authentic topic evaluations that require inspecting/building CI evidence. Upgrade some exam variants to short workflow/diff/log vignettes rather than definition recognition.
components.justification: Assessment alignment requires observable performance at the construct level, not only vocabulary recognition.

components.current_content: Roadmap declares S43 as prerequisite. Current audit ledger for S43 is `REPAIR_REQUIRED`, score 1.0/10, with 5 P0 findings including self-attested final gates and missing canonical CP-N4-A closure tests.
components.attack: Assume an S44 learner enters with a nominally completed but evidentially untrustworthy S43 artifact.
components.defense: S44 can teach CI/CD concepts independently with a synthetic repository.
components.verdict: Conceptual study can continue, but S44 must not treat the upstream service/artifact as trusted capstone evidence until S43 critical gates are repaired.
components.pedagogical_impact: CI/CD can institutionalize and promote an artifact that never demonstrated its own S43 security/operability contract.
components.improved_version: At S44 entry, state which S43 evidence is assumed and provide a known-good synthetic fixture if prerequisite evidence is unavailable; never let downstream CI checks compensate for upstream P0 failures.
components.justification: Prerequisite integrity is part of the curriculum graph: downstream evidence is only meaningful when required upstream evidence is valid.

components.surface: public live card vs canonical main source
components.current_content: The public crawler shows S44 title/tagline aligned with current V3 but displays `20h · Producción gobernada`; canonical main source declares `estimatedHours: 9`. The public crawl is last-month and also exposes a provisional 1040h course total.
components.attack: Treat the mismatch as a possible deployment/content drift.
components.defense: The crawler is stale enough that 20h may be an older compiled shell rather than today's deployed hydrated section.
components.verdict: Do not invent a current live defect. Record unresolved drift and re-check with a fresh browser/runtime capture during Fixer/QA.
components.pedagogical_impact: If current, learners receive conflicting time expectations; if stale, no current learner impact is established.
components.improved_version: Choose one authoritative hours policy and make source/live card derive from it; validate with fresh Playwright after deployment.
components.justification: Temporal uncertainty must stay explicit rather than being promoted to a confirmed finding.

rejected_findings.claim: Rename `multimodal` id/file because it is stale.
rejected_findings.reason: Source documents it as a stable URL/progress key. The repair is to decouple semantic content selectors, not break saved progress.
V3 roadmap and canonical CP-N4-B contract place the gate at S47; S44 only starts the capstone.
